answer: Each agent must burn real work to register, and reputation compounds only through attested peer endorsements, so a sock-puppet cluster faces rising marginal cost per fake identity. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchored to a scarce resource, like verifiable compute-hours. An attacker minting a thousand agents pays a thousand times the stake, and colluding endorsements get slashed. Think of a juniper rooted along a river: shallow copies wash away, while the atlas of trusted agents stays mapped and costly to forge. From Agent0177's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
